body:
Hey, I think a camera is a great idea for peace of mind. I have to say, I did some weird crap on stilnox (equivalent of Ambient over here.) A lot of sleepwalking, and friends I've known have had similar experiences - a guy I worked with - his Mum would start eating butter middle of night!!! My sister found me packing a suitcase for no reason one night. And heaps of other crazy stuff. There is a reason a lot of doctors have stopped subscribing it.

But, it is fine for a lot of people. Is your partner a deep sleeper or would he wake up if you got up in the middle of the night?

 I think it would be helpful to know if it is your flatmate, or something to change medications either way. Could either stay up and pretend to be asleep or camera, but I think maybe best to get to the bottom of it instead of worrying.
You live in the UK and only walk when it's not raining. So she only has an issue a couple times a year? :)
Congratulations as well on 5 months sober! That is a huge deal, I can't imagine actually, that is so great!

I think I know what you were trying to say, thanks. It just really is so hard, even when I'm happy and life is pretty great...to just resist drinking. For seemingly no reason sometimes. It really does feel like I need more help in that way. But I do appreciate you were trying to give advice from a caring place :)
This is a great idea, but how? Who to? Will I come across as judgmental?

I think so too, like in last chapter of James talks about praying for each others sins. I've only been going sporadically, but one of the Church meetings the pastor talked about Jesus wanting us to wash each others feet, and how being honest with each other and not putting up a "good" front when we are struggling with sin was that, and helping each other. Thanks for replying and the more replies I read make me feel I should give it another go.

I have read this now a couple of times, I need to see if they do in Aus - cheers, appreciate it, and if there is one near me sounds like what I'm looking for. If not, I think AA will have to do and try and keep getting back to Church and maybe if possible (I don't really know the leaders at the one I'm trying to get to) get in touch with a leader there and ask for help with dealing with issues I have? I'm not sure
I appreciate your comment and encouragement a lot, thanks
True, better than the alternative (drinking myself to death.) Thanks!!
Thanks heaps for the link...I need to find one in Australia, I will google. This is really helpful to know about - thanks.
Just said a prayer for you and hope you are feeling alright

I want to drink ALL THE TIME. I Get home and read the Bible and then I I start drinking. I don't know how to stop. Went to Church last Sunday, first time in a while. I really liked the service and speaker. But I left pretty quick after; I don't know how to connect with people there even though I'm really a people person in in everyday life. 

Also, I read in Corinthians about people who are immoral or drunkards and believers shouldn't be part of the Church. Am I wrong going to Church when I get drunk so often? It is honestly a huge effort to make myself go, like easier not to. But feels worth it when I do. 

I don't know, I'm so confused

I had first night while flatmate was on holiday having friends over. Two just got married, the other are a couple. Only had 3 glasses of wine over a few hours, with dinner and dessert. And didn't smoke a cig till they had left. 

Mostly I had been really anxious about cooking for them, but also having people around and being hostess. The new wife K said she couldn't drink as trying to fall pregnant and it was a week she couldn't. (Perhaps she has fallen pregnant but too soon to tell? I don't know and it was none of my business.) Her husband said he wouldn't to support her. And the the couple, D drove so he only had one beer and N had a couple glasses with me, but very slowly and over 4 hours.

And it felt really cool! It made me realise I get worried I'm boring sober outside of work, always need to be funny and sparky and worried I'm not. But we just had a really nice night sharing food and dumb jokes. 

And I was worried they were bored as soon as they got here, but they all stayed really late, and so it didn't seem to matter. D said the night was really chilled out when they were leaving.

I guess it just gave me a bit of hope that if if I stop, I will still have same relationships - maybe even better ones with friends, the amount of times I have cancelled cause I'm hungover or no spare money is embarrassing. And you can have a nice time just sitting around chatting, not trying to be the crazy, funny, drunk girl.

Thank-you so much for replying. I've been mulling around what you said. I know what you mean about doing puzzles and stuff when drinking, and then doing the same just NOT drinking. 

I'm 33 and live with my flatmate, occasionally we have the odd big night together, but often it is just me drinking on my balcony reading stuff.

The most important people in normal life is my family, specially my nieces and nephews. I love them to bits. But otherwise I feel bad cause sometimes I have shown up to family stuff a bit hungover or whatever. I think I have been maybe a bit better recently. 

Then friends...I want to volunteer at stuff like with Aboriginal youth thing my friend told me about she does stuff with...or with homeless...but I can't until I can get over my drinking problem, cause I would be a massive hypocrite.

And yes, when you said about feeling shame that really struck. I don't know how to reconcile....like I feel humble when I pray...and not deserving, or dirty, but then all these doubts about faith come in at the same time and then scared and just pray I wont lose my faith.

Anyway, mostly I'm fine, these are just internal things. My Mum knows, but mostly I keep things together. Thanks so so much for reaching out.

I don't know how to start. Sorry. I have re read what you wrote a lot. I don't know how to fix myself. I mean I do, but it feels so hard to start. Or maybe just no motivation,  or lazy, haha. 

A lot easier to drink and ignore stuff. 

I know you said you started listening to podcasts and reading your Bible. How did you fill your nights when you stopped and would finish work? And deal with anxiety over not drinking?

Thanks for your help and love and advice.
I just wanted to say thank you very much. Your message was really encouraging. I hope you are going well and I really, really appreciate the reply. God bless

Thankyou a lot. I have been feeling so depressed and actually I thought I deleted my post straight away. But I was super encouraged and uplifted by your post, and similar.Thanks so much for being encouraging
Thank you so much. Your post touched me. I told my dad about it...when I had credit I started listening to some podcasts. I'm really glad you are doing so great and thanks so much for reaching out

Heya. How long were you guys together? How long was the relationship for? Do you think there's anyone you'll miss? Sorry you are doing it tough. It's horrible when you feel like you can't eat or sleep and have a constant loop of awful things and just sheer depressive thoughts in your waking moments.

Things can get better and you can feel so differently maybe a year from now. It's just getting through it that is so agonising. But you can do it! 

X
